lines: I should get back to edges and balance. A blade owes someone its <pulse>truth</pulse>.
Best I return to sharpening before the forge turns cold.
There is a handle and guard waiting for their final fit.
I promised to finish one clean edge before the hour is out.
I have steel to listen to and tools to quiet.
A customer is still waiting on a repair.
That edge needs one last pass on the stone.
If the forge cools now, I lose half the afternoon.
Talk can wait. The loose guard cannot.
I left a handle clamped at the bench.
The tools are exactly where the work stopped.
I should finish the repair before the light changes.
An unfinished blade makes poor company.
The hammer has been quiet long enough.
I have a fitting to test before supper.
That customer has waited patiently. I should reward the miracle.
Steel remembers when a smith gets distracted.
I need to check the balance while the handle is still warm.
The forge is calling, and it is less polite than you.
Back to work before the edge suffers for my conversation.
